chapter: The Famous Door, Billy May and the Palomar fire
title: The Famous Door band at the Palomar: new trombonist Spud Murphy
summary: The Palomar band was the Famous Door band with a few changes, including Spud Murphy on first trombone and a new drummer.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: I imagine. Have we skipped anything between the -- between '37 and '39?
Well, not really. I mean we had, you know, a rather haphazard existence until the Famous Door. It was an in and out situation.
Was the Famous Door after the Palomar?
So it was -- was it essentially the same band from the Famous Door that got to the Palomar?

Yeah, it was the same band, with you know, a few minor changes. We had a different drummer, and there had been a couple of changes, one change in the trumpet section and one in the saxophone section, oh, and one in the trombone section. We had gotten Lyle, "Spud" Murphy, for the first trombone, which we needed badly, because none of the

guys we had in the Famous Door was really a first trombone player and Spud was. And we had strengthened the trumpet section by adding Johnnie Owens, and we had Ray Michaels playing drums, rather than Wes Dean, who was in the Famous Door band. But basically it was the same band, and they'd been together a long time, you know as bands go.
Did Spud Murphy write for your band then?
No. That's a different Spud Murphy.
The one that does the writing is a saxophone player.
